# Yardlet 0.11.0
The first public release of Yardlet, a native macOS app for running coding agents. Codex, Claude Code and other agent CLIs open side by side in one window of projects and tasks, while each agent keeps its own agent loop, sign-in and session history.
This repository used to hold Yardlet's command-line predecessor, a Rust CLI. Its code and releases (v0.10.3 and earlier) stay available on the `legacy-cli` branch and its tags.
## Highlights
- One window for Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor Agent, Antigravity CLI, Kimi Code, Grok Build, Pi and others, each started with the CLI and account you already use. - Sessions stay in each agent's own store, so a task resumes in the original app or CLI and back. - Several accounts per provider, with each account's session and weekly limits. - Review the last turn's diff, restore or fork files, follow a pull request's checks through `gh`, and keep a terminal and files pane beside the conversation. - Connectors for every agent: Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive through Yardlet's built-in MCP server on your Mac, plus GitHub, Slack and remote MCP services. - A built-in Chromium browser the agents can drive while you watch. - Scheduled tasks, and session tools that let one task read, message or start another. - Updates through Sparkle from this release on.
## Install
Download `Yardlet-0.11.0.dmg` below, open it and drag Yardlet to Applications. It is signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Requires macOS 15 or later on Apple silicon, and at least one agent CLI installed and signed in.
## Known limits
- Google connectors: Google is still reviewing Yardlet's access to Gmail, Calendar and Drive. Until it finishes, Google shows an "unverified app" warning when you connect an account, and the built-in Google app accepts a limited number of new accounts. You can use your own Google OAuth client in Settings > Connectors meanwhile. - The phone remote's Android app is not public yet.
